title: Black Granite Pestle,Pestle Only,Replacement Pestle,5.9" Length Polished,Double Head,Use Pestle on Both Ends
description:
About this item
100% Natural Granite Construction:Crafted from premium natural granite stone with zero synthetic materials or additives, this pestle ensures healthy and safe food preparation. Honoring traditional handicraft techniques, its polished surface resists chipping while maintaining authentic grinding efficiency - fits all mortars seamlessly for versatile kitchen use
Double-Headed Reversible Design:Innovative double head pestle features dual-textured ends: both rough grinding surfaces maximize friction for faster spice crushing. The reversible use functionality allows quick switching between coarse grinding (garlic/pepper) and fine milling (herbs/nuts), doubling your kitchen tool efficiency in one compact marble pestle
Ultimate Versatility for Wet & Dry Ingredients:From chunky guacamole to silky pesto, this granite pestle masters both wet and dry tasks. Engineered to crush garlic, ginger, spices, and even ice for cocktails (use as muddler), its weight-balanced black granite pestle body delivers precise control - ideal for replacing worn pestle for mortar sets
Ergonomic Size & Universal Compatibility:With a 5.9-inch length and dual heads (2.24"/1.85" diameters), this pestle only tool nestles perfectly in any standard mortar (1-2mm tolerance). The natural stone pestle’s smooth mid-section ensures secure grip, while its gray/granite pestle finish adds rustic charm to modern kitchens
Lifetime Durability Guarantee :Backed by 24/7 customer support (response within 24 hours), this double end pestle withstands decades of daily use. As a pestle for replacement or standalone upgrade, its black marble pestle integrity stays intact - simply hand-wash and air-dry to maintain its natural granite brilliance
reviews_5s:
A few years ago I found this marble mortar at the thrift store, with no pestle. On a different occasion i found a wooden pestle and I bought that too... but there are only certain things that would be good for and I've never actually used it which means I've never gotten any use out of the mortar either. I really wanted a stone one. This granite pestle obviously does not match my mortar in color or in size. It seems designed more for a Mexican style "molcajete" mortar like you'd use for smashing together guacamole ingredients. I live by myself and only need a smaller serving of guacamole so I will definitely be trying it for that purpose!!

My mortar and this pestle also do not match in Mohs hardness (the measure of hardness of stone): Granite is 8 on the Mohs scale, and marble is 4. I wondered if the granite might tend to scratch the marble (though damaging it is not a huge concern since it was from the thrift store and probably cost a dollar). So far that has not seemed to be an issue at all, and regardless marble is made of calcium and is basically metamorphosed limestone and will not hurt you. Granite

For reference in figuring out whether this is the size you would want a replacement pestle to be, my mortar in the photos is 9.5 cm inside diameter and 11 cm outside diameter (it measures more nearly in centimeters is why I give that unit of measure). This pestle would actually best fit a larger mortar but it is usable with this size.

So far I've tried crushing walnut meats and candy cane very successfully, which made me happy because it's both easier and produces a better result than other methods of crushing those that I've used, e.g., this method neither pulverized walnut unintentionally into a paste or flour nor left large chunks uncrushed. One of the things I have struggled the most in the past to turn it into a paste type texture is dates (which I like to use as a natural sweetener for baked goods, and also I'd love to put them in smoothies but I need to get rid of most of the chunkiness); I need to experiment more on some combination method of chopping and smashing but my trial of smashing up a couple of Deglet Noor dates torn into large pieces was pretty good. I think smashing first then scooping out the pulp and chopping it, before possibly another round of smashing might be the way to go. I did try garlic also but my garlic cloves turned out to be so dessicated that the result was not great. I am confident it would smash fresh garlic cloves quite effectively.

a tip: I discovered crumpled aluminum foil is a good tool for cleaning off the pestle in between using it on peppermint candy and garlic.This granite pestle is awesome. It has just enough texture on both ends to grind REALLY effectively... I say "really" because it pulverized some toasted cumin in maybe half the time my old one did. It's got real heft to it so it's not for you if you're looking for a dainty unit, but i love it because it seems like it does the grinding with very little elbow grease required. Being solid granite it's easy to clean as expected and never transfers flavors in any of the times I've used it. The polished surface feels great in your hand and it looks pretty dang sharp in your kitchen. No complaints here - highly recommended!Sturdy, heavy, and just as pictured. But maybe a little larger than what i neededWe use this to crush various items into baby-food texture: dried nuts into nut powder for allergen exposure, grinding ground beef into finer texture, etc. Our baby went through a gagging/vomiting phase, so this was really helpful to ensure a texture he could handle. This pestle is SUPER solid and heavy duty. Before I was using a wooden dowel and it would take a lot of force. This one is so heavy the weight takes care of most of the crushing. Because of that, I do worry about whatever glass bowl I'm using, but so far I've been very careful and haven't had any issues. Next time I may get a set that includes a mortar so I can crush even harder, but for this standalone item I give 5 stars.A solid pestle that is polished and runs great after I broke it in properly. No chips or damage on mine. Looks good and is easy to use. Good size for most uses and cleans easily if done properly.It works great to grind up the tough stuff! We use it to grind up freeze dried beef liver to sprinkle on our dog’s food, and that stuff is rock hard, but by the time we are done it is dust.
The pestle has a good weight and heft to it, and fits comfortably in your hand. It’s also easy to wash. Well worth the price.Nice and heavy duty, well madeWe got this primarily for making fresh guacamole, but it can be used for a wide variety of things. It's basically just a massive piece of black granite that has been perfectly shaped and polished. It is quite heavy, as it should be, which makes it a lot easier to smash spices, avocados, nuts, or anything else you might be using it for. I would highly recommend it for anyone looking for a pestle for their kitchen. This thing is like a work of art in itself, it will surely help you create some of your own masterpieces as wellHeavy stone pestle features two different shape ends for use with various items. One end is more rounded with the other end being flatter although still a bit rounded to allow it to fit well in the bottom of a mortar. It’s well weighted allowing it to easily crush items from dried spices to grains.Fits my hand very well and is comfortable to hold. It's also a perfect weight for me: heavy enough to help with the chore but not enough to be tiresome. The grip section is polished and smooth while the two grinding ends are smooth but plain stone and unpolished - as they should be. I really appreciate the two different heads with their two different radius' - they allow more variation in purpose. I'm very happy with mine.
